races.name: eventmasters.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's six-year-old has won twice prominently at seven furlongs on good ground in recent starts and is the sole confirmed pace-setter here; Kevin Stott should get a free lead in an 18-runner field, though the STYLE_FIT flag suggests any scenario requiring repositioning would temper confidence.|

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this hold-up type for David O'Meara but a form string of 6-5767 and zero wins or places on similar going in 13 attempts makes improvement hard to argue; the seven furlongs here is longer than the six where most recent runs have been.|

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: A hold-up gelding for O'Meara who has never won or placed on similar going in six attempts, and recent finishes of 6th, 11th and 12th underline the concern; the headgear (hood) has not unlocked the form, and an apprentice claimer reduces the tactical edge.|

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for Iain Jardine who has placed in four of his last five on good ground at six furlongs; stepping up to seven here is the key question, though Jack Nicholls's 5lb claim preserves the handicap weight advantage.|

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Geoffrey Harker's hold-up six-year-old won off a mark at seven furlongs on good ground but has form notes flagging a tendency to fade in the finish; a 38-day break and a step back to seven from longer trips requires a small leap of faith.|

runners_data.name: Stratocracy
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this prominent five-year-old who has won at seven furlongs on standard ground and placed consistently; five previous runs at the trip and a recent third suggest conditions are fine, though five of six recent finishes are 5th or worse.|

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's six-year-old has recorded three wins at seven-to-eight furlongs on good ground this season and arrives in excellent form (112113); prominent style suits this race shape ideally and Connor Beasley's local knowledge is an asset.|

runners_data.name: Quest For Fun
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's eight-year-old has placed twice at seven furlongs on good ground but three blanks in the last four runs and a 0W record in similar conditions dampen enthusiasm; the prominent tag fits the shape but the age and recent form don't.|

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Another Easterby prominent type who placed at six furlongs on good ground earlier in the season; the switch to seven furlongs is a small step up in trip and recent form (870320) has been mixed, but the style suits the expected shape.|

runners_data.name: Golden Strike
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's five-year-old won at seven furlongs on good ground and has two placed efforts on similar surfaces; visor retained, 27-day break is fine, and prominent racing style places him exactly where the pace map rewards horses.|

runners_data.name: Monsieur Bondy
runners_data.note: Geoff Oldroyd's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up type who won at seven furlongs on standard ground but has run poorly on good going in four of five attempts; PJ McDonald takes over but form at the trip on today's surface remains thin.|

runners_data.name: Royal Accord
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer with two wins at six furlongs on good ground, but a 283-day absence and the fact that more prominent types than can realistically hold their position exist in this field are real concerns; Silvestre De Sousa's quality helps if the return to fitness is genuine.|

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's ten-year-old has a natural desire to race prominently but this veteran has been squeezed into a midfield map position because the field is simply overloaded with pace types; recent form of 60027 at six furlongs and a 51-day absence make the handicap task steep.|

runners_data.name: Orne
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's five-year-old is a hold-up type with placed efforts at seven furlongs on good ground and wears blinkers; a 42-day gap and inconsistent form (03037) mean the profile is interesting for a late-running scenario without being convincing.|

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has a genuine hold-up style backed by consistent placed form (731342) including a win at seven furlongs on good ground; however, the field density means this horse is mapped to midfield rather than its natural rearward berth, which could compromise the trademark late finish.|

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old owns three wins on good ground at six furlongs and is in excellent recent form (004131); though mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear, the natural hold-up approach has produced results at a shorter trip and the seven furlongs here is unproven.|

runners_data.name: Intervention
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's nine-year-old has not won or placed on similar going in six attempts and a form line of 400877 leaves no reason for optimism; mapped to midfield rather than its natural hold-up position, and the age and trajectory suggest marginal involvement.|

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's four-year-old has won twice at six furlongs on good ground in recent form (831134) and wears a visor; a natural hold-up runner placed into midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear, and the step up to seven furlongs here is the key unknown for what has been a sharp, short-trip type.|

races.paceDynamic: Alpha Capture is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to take them on for the lead, should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop down the centre of York's straight seven furlongs on good-to-firm ground. The pace will be honest but controlled — Alpha Capture's rider Kevin Stott can dictate terms and set a rhythm that suits horses travelling prominently behind, with Jonny Concrete, Stratocracy, Roaring Ralph, Quest For Fun, Mister Sox and Golden Strike all likely to press forward into the slipstream. Critically, Royal Accord, Fortamour and the redistributed hold-up horses Ashen, Invincible Ruby, Intervention and Jet Warrior are unlikely to secure their natural positions given the volume of prominent-minded types in this field, compressing the midfield and leaving true closers with less daylight than ideal. The race shape — a sustainable gallop with a well-organised prominent pack — strongly favours horses who race in the first four or five and can quicken off a steady but uncontested tempo, making prominent racers the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent pack travels smoothly throughout the seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: Alpha Capture dictates a comfortable pace, allowing horses like Roaring Ralph, Golden Strike and Jonny Concrete to track closely and produce their finishing efforts from a position of comfort; on good-to-firm York ground this shape consistently rewards those who travel close to the pace without burning energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture's uncontested lead allows it to conserve enough energy to simply run the field ragged at its own pace.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied, Alpha Capture could dictate a tempo that is deceptively strong yet feels comfortable, stealing a decisive break turning into the final two furlongs and holding on as the field fails to coordinate a coherent chase.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string out the field and leave something for hold-up types who find a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: Ashen and Orne have the profile of horses that can pick up ground in the final furlong when the prominent runners tire, and on fast ground York's long straight can allow late runs to materialise; however, several nominally hold-up runners are not true closers and this scenario is discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 18-runner field causes significant traffic issues, a messy early order or a slow pace that bunches the field and produces an unpredictable sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a compressed field with no pressure on the leader, a late sprint could elevate a fresh hold-up type or an unexposed runner; however, this scenario depends on the field failing to organise itself, which is less likely when there is one clear pace-setter with a settled front position.

watchPoints.text: Roaring Ralph arrives in career-best form (112113) with three wins at the trip on good ground this season — if Beasley slots him prominently behind the leader, he is the most dangerous horse in the race for the dominant scenario.

Alpha Capture has a lone front-running profile in a flat, straight seven — watch whether Stott is allowed a completely uncontested lead, as even a length of daylight could prove decisive given the horse's good-ground record at the trip.

Royal Accord returns from 283 days off and, despite strong course-and-distance form, the absence length combined with being squeezed from a natural prominent position by a congested pace group could see it outrun early and finish flat.

Jet Warrior and Invincible Ruby are both mapped to midfield against their natural rear-running instincts — in a race where the midfield is already crowded, watch for traffic issues in the final two furlongs that could frustrate both horses' finishing runs.

Golden Strike and Mister Sox both carry similar profiles (prominent, good-to-firm form) for the same Fahey/Easterby yards at similar weights — if either drifts in the betting late, it may signal a stable preference or fitness concern worth noting before post time.

races.name: Elevator Company Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Uncontested lead expected here; Bethell has 5 wins from 30 in the past 14 days and apprentice Cian Horgan takes off valuable weight — the key question is whether front-running form over shorter trips translates to 2m½f, but the style fit on a flat track is solid.

runners_data.name: Midnight Rumble
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator whose best form is on good ground and over staying trips, but 0 wins from 15 similar-going runs is a red flag; Rob Hornby can ride a waiting game but needs either a strong pace or a lucky passage through 14 rivals.

runners_data.name: Venezuelan
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in a visor who finished second twice on similar going and handles this sort of trip, though four runs without a win lately suggest he may be running into form rather than out of it; Jack Nicholls (5) is a booking for a trainer who fires horses fit.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance experience is the standout credential here — won over 14f on good at this track recently; Paul Mulrennan is a booking Jim Goldie uses when he fancies his chance, and the hood (hg:p) has been worn in winning runs.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who won over a mile on standard at Dundalk but has struggled on good turf in bigger fields recently; Oisin Orr is a strong claimer-less booking but the tongue-tie (hg:t) has not sparked a revival and OR=74 reflects a horse on a downward curve.

runners_data.name: Rogue Empire
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins heading into this, including two on good and two over 2m — the profile fits the race shape perfectly; Owen Lewis (5) takes weight off and Roger Teal has just 0/9 in the past 14 days, but the horse's own form is the compelling factor here.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on good last time and has placed four times at 16f, showing he stays; Kieran Shoemark is a high-quality retention and a blinker runner who won without headgear last time — that combination warrants scrutiny.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with wins over 16f on good ground who is a natural front-runner by trade, but the field is too full of prominent types to allow him to express that — he's been pushed into a midfield slot on the map that doesn't suit his instincts, and the STYLE_FIT tag tempers his chance accordingly; Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form (T14:8/68).

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up mare with a 1W3P record on good ground, handled well by Joanna Mason who knows her patterns; a bold front-runner is the last thing she wants but she has tactical pace at this trip and went in over 11f on good here last time.

runners_data.name: Vaguely Royal
runners_data.note: William Buick's presence on a 69-rated horse in a 14-runner field is the headline angle; won last over 14f on good, placed three more times at Group/Listed level trips, and the visor (hg:v) has featured in placed efforts — a live outsider if Buick finds daylight.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner who is actually pushed further forward on the map than his true style warrants — one placed effort from 10 on similar going and no wins in this company make the task steep; Rhys Elliott (5) takes off weight but the horse has been beaten out of sight in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on good last time and the form trajectory is improving — three places in her last four — but stepping into a 14-runner handicap at 2m½f is a significant class and stamina test; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) is a useful claimer and the horse is lightly weighted.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Experienced stayer with a win and a second over 16f on good ground, but a natural prominent racer who simply cannot get close enough to the pace in this field — the redistribution flag captures the structural problem; Iain Jardine has been firing (T14:2/16) and a wind op (hg:b) was worn in winning form.

runners_data.name: Queen Roslyn
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who has been mapped forward against her natural tendencies because the rear is congested — her best form is on soft ground and her recent two runs on good produced 10th and 11th; Cam Hardie is a capable jockey but the going concern and out-of-role placement both work against her.

races.paceDynamic: Talismans Time is the lone confirmed front-runner and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — the redistributed prominent types (Treasure Islands, Newport) are unlikely to secure their natural positions in a 14-runner field this congested, meaning Talismans Time can control tempo from the front without being harried. At 2m½f on Good to Firm ground at York, a horse allowed to dictate at a fair but uncontested gallop sets a premium on relaxed travelling and a sustained late effort rather than a sharp finishing kick, favouring those who can hold a handy position without burning energy early. The field contains significant traffic risk in the midfield and rear, where genuine hold-up horses (Valley Of Flowers, Vaguely Royal, Midnight Rumble) must find a clear run over the final quarter-mile. Several redistributed runners — Treasure Islands, Newport, Furhaan, Queen Roslyn — are mapped out of their true positions because the prominent berths are already full, and their true styles are constrained by the race shape. This race shape strongly favours prominent, pace-pressing types who can track Talismans Time at close quarters without overexerting, as the controlled gallop will not soften the ground sufficiently to produce a true staying test that brings hold-up horses into their own.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Press Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time sets an uncontested, honest gallop and the race is won from the front two or three throughout.
scenarios.body: Talismans Time dictates from the front with Rogue Empire or Tarbat Ness pressing at a respectful distance, and the lead group simply never relinquishes enough to allow closers to make meaningful ground; the good-to-firm surface rewards horses who travel prominently without the fractions being punishing enough to bring them back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time sets a genuinely strong clip that stretches the field and gives hold-up types a faint chance to pounce.
scenarios.body: The pace is hot enough to bring the lead group back in the final furlong, allowing Valley Of Flowers or Vaguely Royal, who travel well in midfield, to pick up the pieces with a sustained run; William Buick on Vaguely Royal or Joanna Mason on Valley Of Flowers would need clear daylight through the pack, which is not guaranteed at 2m½f with 14 runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If chaos at the start or traffic bunching forces the prominent horses wide and creates a scrambled race for position.
scenarios.body: Horses pushed out of their ideal early positions — particularly the redistributed Newport or Treasure Islands — are already operating at a disadvantage, but a messy race could neutralise the front-runners' structural advantage and reward whoever threads through cleanest; Trojan Sun, who showed form over this C&D trip and handles good ground, is the most likely beneficiary in a chaotic shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the field converges in a muddling, slowly-run finish.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on hold-up horses who have already been redistributed out of their true rear positions (Furhaan, Queen Roslyn) reversing the race shape, which is unlikely given their out-of-role placement and modest ORs; Midnight Rumble, the one genuine hold-up type on an unrestricted map, represents the best prospect here, though the flat York straight offers limited scope for dramatic late recovery at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Empire (three-timer attempt, OR=74, prominent style in a single front-runner race) is the most dangerous pace-pressing type in the field and could be on Talismans Time's shoulder throughout — watch whether Owen Lewis sends him forward immediately from the gates.

Traffic congestion in the midfield is a significant risk for Vaguely Royal and Valley Of Flowers — William Buick and Joanna Mason will need clear runs in a 14-runner field over this trip, and a pocket could easily end either chance before the final two furlongs.

Treasure Islands and Newport, natural front-runners redistributed into midfield, could cause interference if they attempt to push up towards their preferred position from a wider draw in the early stages — watch for restlessness and jostling entering the first bend.

Tarbat Ness is running in blinkers (hg:b) after winning without them last time — headgear changes mid-sequence in stayers can alter early pace behaviour and it is worth monitoring whether Kieran Shoemark sends him forward more aggressively than his form pattern suggests.

Going update confirms Good to Firm for this race specifically — any market moves for horses with a strong good-ground record (Rogue Empire, Trojan Sun, Tarbat Ness) should be weighted accordingly, as the surface will reward travelling smoothly rather than grinding.

races.name: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Diplomacy
runners_data.note: Unexposed two-year-old with unknown style who carries the lightly-raced flag; Billy Garritty holds a decent claim here, and the Easterby yard is operating at a modest 3/26 over 14 days, so the form lines offer little to work with — treat as a genuine each-way unknown who could slot anywhere positionally.

runners_data.name: Rule Of The Agency
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner posted a seventh on Good 8f last time and holds a genuine hold-up profile; the field's density forces it forward off its preferred deep position, meaning it races partially against its own grain — 38 days off the track adds a mild fitness query.

runners_data.name: The First Drop
runners_data.note: Keatley's runner is the race's sole confirmed front-runner after a placed effort over this exact 7f trip on Good ground last time, and should coast to an uncontested lead from the gates; the pace it sets will shape every other horse's fortune, and its STYLE_FIT tag reflects that truly dictating suits it more than being pressured.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Rocket
runners_data.note: A fader at the finish on its only start (eighth, 7f, Good) and carries a clear stamina concern over this trip; Joanna Mason takes a 3lb claim but the horse's tendency to find nothing late is a structural negative regardless of position, and 18 days since that run gives little time for improvement.

runners_data.name: Special Operations
runners_data.note: Completely unraced debutant for Tim Easterby — the Kirrane booking is workmanlike, the trainer's yard is busy, and with zero public form lines the style profile is labelled unknown; could be anything, and any positional reading is speculative.

runners_data.name: Sweet Iris
runners_data.note: Fahey's filly finished last of ten over 6f on Good ground 18 days ago and showed a fade pattern that is now a concern; stepping up to 7f is logical on pedigree but she has yet to prove she handles the extra distance, and her hold-up profile may leave her too much to do if the pace is not truly searching.

runners_data.name: Travellers Girl
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's filly has a tidy record of three placed efforts from three runs, all over 6f on Good ground — the step up to 7f today is the key unknown; Kevin Stott is a sharp operator and the OR=70 conceals a consistent profile, but the trip extension is a real question mark she must answer.

runners_data.name: Coral Cove
runners_data.note: James Owen's runner posted a creditable second over this exact 7f trip on Good ground and Kieran Shoemark is an upgrade booking; a prominent style suits the likely race shape perfectly, and 34 days since that run means she arrives fresh enough to build on it.

races.paceDynamic: The going report confirms Good To Firm throughout the afternoon at York, and this 7f novice is set up around a single confirmed pace-setter: The First Drop, who slots in as the lone front-runner and should control proceedings from the gates without any genuine pressure to burn off. Coral Cove will sit prominently just behind, and with no rival willing to challenge The First Drop for the lead, the tempo is likely to be honest but controlled rather than truly searching — exactly the kind of race where a well-positioned horse stalking the pace can pounce without burning energy. The race shape therefore favours horses who can race prominently or within two lengths of the pace through the first four furlongs, since the lack of pressure at the front means late closers from deep may find the winner long gone. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate: Rule Of The Agency and The Resdev Rocket are genuine hold-up horses who will be racing against their natural grain, and it is The First Drop and Coral Cove who are most likely to actually secure their intended positions and benefit from the shape they create.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If The First Drop is allowed to bowl along uncontested and dictates a sustainable gallop with Coral Cove tracking.
scenarios.body: The First Drop sets a manageable pace and, never having burned excessive energy, finds extra in the final two furlongs on this flat, quick surface; Coral Cove, tracking the leader throughout, is ideally placed to challenge but may lack the finishing burst to overhaul a fresh front-runner with a lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo proves just lively enough to peg The First Drop back inside the final furlong, allowing a close tracker to swoop.
scenarios.body: Coral Cove or one of the unexposed runners (Diplomacy, Special Operations) sits a length or two off the pace, conserves energy through the middle section, and produces a decisive move when the leader idles; on quick going at York the flat track gives no hiding place and a sharp turn of foot is rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Runs Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the principals and a horse from the middle of the pack finds clear daylight late.
scenarios.body: Rule Of The Agency or Sweet Iris, operating out of their preferred hold-up position but still arriving with momentum in the final furlong, benefits if the front pair have burned each other; this scenario is discounted because neither horse is genuinely operating as a pure closer today and the pace is not forecast to be truly pressured.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is too slow and several horses sprint from far out, creating a bunched, scrappy finish.
scenarios.body: Travellers Girl, stepping up from 6f with solid placed form on similar going, could outrun her OR=70 in a messy sprint to the line; Special Operations, completely unexposed, is a wildcard whose unknown profile could suit any shape, including this unpredictable one.

watchPoints.text: The First Drop's uncontested lead is the race's central structural fact — if Shoemark on Coral Cove attempts to push up and challenge early, it could compromise both front horses and open the race significantly.

Rule Of The Agency is a genuine hold-up horse forced forward by race shape; if David Allan attempts to drop it in regardless and traffic builds mid-pack, it may find no passage in a small eight-runner field.
Travellers Girl steps up 1f in trip having run exclusively over 6f — watch the market move as the key indicator of whether connections believe the extra distance suits before dismissing the outsider.

The Resdev Rocket and Sweet Iris both showed fade patterns on their only respective starts and are confirmed hold-up types; if neither can make meaningful ground inside the final two furlongs, it confirms the race is playing to prominent runners throughout.

Special Operations is a well-bred Easterby debutant with no public form — any unusual paddock behaviour or early market support should be logged as it represents genuine unknown upside in an otherwise form-readable field.

races.name: Tomahawk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose recent 6f Good record is excellent (four wins at the trip); controls this from stall one but faces 21 rivals and a weight of 135lbs — if pressured early, will she sustain? Roger Fell yard going well (1/17 T14).

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partnership is a strong angle but this horse's 5f form dominates the history — stepping to 6f on Good to Firm York; a true hold-up type who will need a strong pace to make a late impression from the rear.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse with modest recent form (17th, 10th in last two starts); 41 days off and his similar-going record shows no wins from 15 attempts, making it hard to make a case at these odds.

runners_data.name: Raatea
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has shown ability onStandside/Fibresand but has zero wins from six similar-going runs and arrives 134 days off — a significant layoff that introduces fitness doubt for an already outpaced hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Almarada Prince
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a solid recent run (4th at 6f Good, 3rd at 6f Good) — Paul Mulrennan can read a race and this horse's placed form on Good going makes him a midfield danger if gaps emerge.

runners_data.name: Aberama Gold
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old but lively form — back-to-back 2nds at 6f Good in recent outings, headgear (visor), and David O'Meara's yard firing (5/43 T14); though a hold-up type mapped to midfield, his finishing speed has been consistent.

runners_data.name: HK Fourteen
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's six-year-old has strong 5f form and three wins on Good going in his history; racing over 6f here, he'll need to settle prominently and his T14 rate of 5/31 suggests the yard is in decent form.

runners_data.name: Rajaking
runners_data.note: Well-handicapped at OR 76 with a win and multiple places at 6f Good; Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking but the horse's natural hold-up style means he'll need traffic to part in the straight to unleash his finishing run.

runners_data.name: Magic Boy
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald aboard a horse who has won twice and placed seven times on Good going — excellent record on the surface, races prominently, and his recent 1st and 2nd at 6f/7f confirm he is in form at OR 76.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's seven-year-old has a strong 6f Good profile with a win and five placings from nine attempts; prominent racer who will be ideally placed, though a 0 on the last run is a minor concern over this trip.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in the finish, has had a 168-day absence, and his form at 7f on Standard/All-Weather dominates — the trip drop to 6f on Good to Firm turf does not obviously suit this hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Alpha Magic
runners_data.note: Trainer Michael & David Easterby have 3/26 in T14 window; this four-year-old's form shows a string of mid-field finishes on Good (11th, 12th, 8th) and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot — the redistribution limits its scope, and the fading-in-finish flag is a further worry.

runners_data.name: Bonnie's Boy
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey yard running well (4/40 T14) and this four-year-old has shown speed at 5f on Standside previously; a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield out of role, his best chance depends on finding daylight in a crowded finish.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 5f and 7f Good recently show he is in career-best form; runs in headgear (p) and is a genuine hold-up type occupying midfield on the map — if he secures a clear run, he is the most dangerous of the hold-up contingent.

runners_data.name: Beattie Is Back
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a win and a place on Good going at 6f in recent form; Warren Fentiman (3) takes the ride for the Fahey yard — a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield, and the apprentice claiming is a modest compensation in a race where position will be hard to find.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls' five-year-old has three wins and eight placings from 15 Good-going starts — an excellent strike rate at this venue and going; races prominently and should travel into contention from a handy slot.

runners_data.name: Sugar Baby
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won four times and placed six times on Good going from 15 attempts — strong surface profile; races prominently and Peter Niven's horse at OR 71 is potentially well-treated if form figures are taken at face value.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: Four-year-old returning 13 days later; form shows 14th and 10th in recent 6f Good starts — a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations; the trip and going look manageable but recent finishes are unpromising.

runners_data.name: Dicko The Legend
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's six-year-old runs in headgear (p) and ran just 7 days ago; five consecutive placings at 6f Good suggest consistency without a win, and as a hold-up horse occupying a midfield slot he will need pace to suit and a clear run to show his best.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's six-year-old has a very limited record on Good going (four runs, no wins or places at similar going) — poor surface fit; a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map and the combination of going concern and out-of-role position makes this a difficult race.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's in-form yard (8/68 T14) gives this six-year-old a trainer angle; consistent placed form (three 3rds on Good recently) in headgear (p), but the step up from 5f to 6f is a query and as a hold-up type mapped to midfield, he'll need pace to finish over.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Recent winner (2nd and 1st at 6f Good in last two) and runs in tongue-tie; Liam Bailey yard and Billy Garritty sibling pairing; a genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield, but the form entitles him to respect if he secures a forward enough position — ran just 7 days ago like stable companion Dicko.

races.paceDynamic: Glory Hyde is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 22-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can control the tempo from the front on Good to Firm ground at York over 6f. HK Fourteen, Magic Boy, Fiscal Policy, Ingleby Archie and Sugar Baby will press from prominent positions just behind, creating a competitive but not chaotic pace scenario — sustainable enough that the lead is not burned away, but busy enough that the leaders will be tested in the final two furlongs. The field contains an unusually heavy concentration of hold-up horses — Alpha Magic, Who Wants Me, Bonnie's Boy, Beattie Is Back, Educating Rita, Dicko The Legend, Tough Enough, Spirit Of Applause and Dorney Lake are all genuine rear-of-field types redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply insufficient space at the back for all of them, meaning several will race in unnatural positions and their finishing kicks will be compromised. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours prominent racers who can track the pace from a handy position and sustain their effort through the final furlong, rather than hold-up horses who face a crowded, traffic-laden journey from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Glory Hyde sets a fair gallop and the prominent trio of Magic Boy, Fiscal Policy and Ingleby Archie track closely, the race unfolds as a test of sustained speed from the front half.
scenarios.body: Glory Hyde controls from flag to finish while Magic Boy, Ingleby Archie and Fiscal Policy race up to challenge in the final 2f on fast ground that suits their cruising speed; horses from midfield or rear lack the clear run needed to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Weakens, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Glory Hyde's pace is just sharp enough to soften the field but she fades inside the final furlong, a close-tracking prominent horse swoops.
scenarios.body: Sugar Baby or HK Fourteen, sitting just off the pace, pounce as the leader ties up; their prior 6f York form on similar going gives them the edge over rivals arriving from deeper.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn each other off and gaps open in the straight, a well-placed midfield horse with a strong finishing run profits.
scenarios.body: Aberama Gold or Almarada Prince, racing from the rear of the prominent group, benefit from a slightly stronger pace and produce a late surge; their good-going form at 6f is the key credential.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Sprints Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field fans wide in the straight, freeing a back-marker to produce an unimpeded late run.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given so many genuine hold-up horses are occupying midfield out of role and will block each other's finishing runs; only a horse like Who Wants Me or Dorney Lake finding an immediate gap could deliver.

watchPoints.text: Glory Hyde sets the entire race tempo alone — if she is allowed a soft lead, the prominent horses behind her will coast and the hold-up runners will have no pace to chase; watch her early position and how hard she is pressed in the first 2f.

With at least eight genuine hold-up horses competing for midfield slots, significant traffic congestion is probable from the 2f pole — watch for Dicko The Legend, Spirit Of Applause and Beattie Is Back potentially blocking each other's finishing runs.

Magic Boy has an outstanding Good-going record (2W/7P from 10 runs) and PJ McDonald's ability to find a prominent position in a big field makes him a primary beneficiary if the pace scenario plays out cleanly — his draw and early positioning are key.

Who Wants Me is in career-best form with back-to-back wins but must overcome a forced midfield position out of his natural hold-up role — if Andrew Mullen can nurse him through traffic, his raw form entitles him to a place, but a stop-start run is the real risk.

The Good to Firm going confirmed across all York races today could sharpen up finishing times — horses with proven top-speed figures on fast turf (Magic Boy sim-going 10/10; Ingleby Archie 12/15; Sugar Baby 12/15) should be prioritised over those with limited similar-going evidence.

races.name: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Diamond Rain
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 5yo is proven at this sort of trip and trips up to 10-11f, has won at this level before, and Buick gives her every chance to dictate — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is fractionally out of her most comfortable range as a natural prominent racer rather than a true front-runner, but the absence of pressure makes that irrelevant here; she arrives 28 days fresh and handles Good ground.

runners_data.name: Miss Justice
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 5yo is the most natural companion at the head of affairs and represents the only runner whose position on the map is genuinely aligned with her role — she has a troubled recent record (four placed or beaten efforts) at 12f on Good ground and Paul Mulrennan needs a clean trip, but she could benefit from Diamond Rain softening the pace.

runners_data.name: Qilin Queen
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 4yo is the only true hold-up type in the field, and that makes her structurally the best-placed runner to exploit a leader who ties up — Kieran Shoemark rides her for an in-form yard (10/42 last 14 days), she won over 12f on Soft but her seventh here on Good last time is a concern worth noting; distance stamina is not in question.

runners_data.name: Regal Charm
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's 4yo has won twice recently, including over 10f on Soft, and carries strong recent form (1302-1) — instinctively a prominent racer, she has been pushed to midfield on the map simply because the front is already crowded, though she may press forward regardless; 45 days off and only 1 from 6 on similar ground tempers enthusiasm slightly.

runners_data.name: Estissa
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo is lightly raced and progressive over shorter (multiple wins at 8f), making this 10f trip and Listed company a significant step up — Harry Davies takes the ride for a trainer firing at 4/17 in 14 days, and while she is naturally a prominent type, she has been mapped to midfield because she cannot hold that position here; stamina over this trip on fast ground is unproven.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo has won at 8f on Good and 7f on Standard, and while she showed ability at 12f on Soft (seventh), this Good to Firm 10f trip is a different test — Edward Greatrex rides for a trainer in strong form (12/43), but as a naturally prominent type shuffled back by field composition, her ability to travel kindly in midfield off this pace will determine how dangerous she is late.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Rain is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with William Buick aboard for Charlie Appleby, she is likely to dictate a controlled, measured tempo over this 1m2½f trip on Good to Firm ground — the kind of sustainable gallop that keeps her rivals honest without inviting a cavalry charge. Miss Justice is the only other runner whose mapping places her naturally close to the pace, meaning Diamond Rain faces minimal pressure and can effectively set her own fractions from the front. Three runners — On Message, Estissa, and Regal Charm — are genuine prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the race shape simply cannot accommodate all of them near the front; in reality, one or two may push forward and creep closer to Diamond Rain than the map suggests, but they are unlikely all to secure their natural position. This race shape — a single uncontested leader controlling a modest tempo on fast ground — strongly favours a classy hold-up or late-midfield runner who can settle, travel sweetly, and produce a clean sustained run, with Qilin Queen the only true hold-up type in the field ideally configured for that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diamond Rain Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Rain is allowed to stride along uncontested and set an honest but unforced tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Buick dictates from the front at a pace that suits Diamond Rain's class and stamina, leaving rivals to work through traffic on her terms — she remains fresh to the line and is very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that Diamond Rain ties up, allowing Qilin Queen to produce a powerful late run from off it.
scenarios.body: Qilin Queen's natural hold-up style is perfectly configured for this shape; she settles at the back, travels within herself, and a clean run from the two-furlong pole gives her the best chance of sweeping past.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos At Turn
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed runners push forward to claim their natural position, creating an unexpectedly pressured pace into the home straight.
scenarios.body: With On Message, Estissa, and Regal Charm all instinctively wanting to race prominently, a scrappy mid-race surge could unsettle Diamond Rain's rhythm and compress the field, opening a crack for the most adaptable runner to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class Filly Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate throughout and a well-handicapped, classier runner produces a decisive turn of foot in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A flat, steady tempo with a single surge late suits a horse who possesses an explosive gear change rather than raw stamina; this is a low-probability shape given the likely controlled pace.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Rain — if Buick eases into a slow early gallop completely unopposed, she may never be headed; watch whether any redistributed runner pushes forward to apply even token pressure before the home turn.

Regal Charm and On Message — both instinctively want to race prominently and have the form to justify it; if both push for the same ground approaching the first bend, an early scrimmage could compromise Diamond Rain's rhythm and dramatically alter the race shape.

Qilin Queen — held up last of six, she needs an unobstructed passage from two furlongs out; with only six runners this is achievable, but Shoemark must commit at the right moment or a modest-paced race may simply not produce enough late ground to catch Diamond Rain.

Estissa — keep an eye on how she handles the step up to 10f on fast ground first time at this trip; if she struggles to settle in a role that is not naturally hers, she may fade quickly in the final furlong and traffic the horses behind her.

races.name: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will look to control from the gates; Easterby yard in decent nick (8/68), but 68 days off the track and recent form of 09-454 suggests she gets caught late rather than wins; Good to Firm is fine for her, though the step back to 5½f from 6f is worth noting — her style fit here is limited by the fact that this position is genuinely front-running, not truly prominent.

runners_data.name: Nursia
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan runner returning after 43 days off with just three runs in the book; won on Standard at 6f but her one run on similar Good ground produced only a fifth; Kevin Stott rides and the stable has had just 1 winner from 21 runners in the past fortnight, so keep expectations measured.

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has been placed once in eight runs on similar going; Oisin McSweeney takes the ride for Kevin Ryan, and the 27-day gap since his last run is manageable — the concern is eight runs on good ground producing only one win and two places at shorter trips, suggesting he needs everything to fall right late.

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Consistent David Allan-ridden prominent racer for Tim Easterby who has placed at 5f and 6f on Good ground multiple times (5W2P in sim-going runs); 27 days since last run and OR 80 gives him a fair chance if he settles just off the leader rather than getting drawn into the pace battle.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3yo who won at 5f on Soft and has placed at 5f on Standard; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claim) rides and the trainer's recent 2/5 strike rate is encouraging, but only one placed run in five on good ground and questions about her handling of genuinely quick conditions.

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's prominent-style runner has placed at 5f and 6f on Good ground repeatedly (1W3P sim-going); Harry Davies in the saddle and a 21-day freshener — the yard has drawn a blank in 22 attempts over 14 days, but the horse's own form on this going is the strongest asset here.

runners_data.name: Dolos Dream
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on this horse who has won twice at 5f on Standard and placed at 6f Soft — naturally a front-rank racer, but the crowded prominent contingent means he is unlikely to secure his preferred position and will race in a role that doesn't come naturally; form on strictly Good ground is thin (one run, fifth).

runners_data.name: Bravo Hotel
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides this hold-up type for the Michael & David Easterby yard; three placed efforts at 5f on both Good and Soft ground suggest she is consistent without winning, and 38 days since her last run is the key unknown — she needs a truly run race to get into it.

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr picks up the mount on a horse who has been placed four times in eight runs without winning; form figures of 2-2-3-3 are consistent but the win has proved elusive, and two placed efforts at 5f on Good ground give some hope — the Frost yard sent out one winner from nine runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello's mount has won twice at 5f on Good and placed six times in eleven similar-going runs, making him one of the most course-type-fitting horses in the field; his natural style is to race prominently, and despite the map pushing him to midfield, Costello will almost certainly attempt to get forward — whether he can slot in near the pace depends on how aggressively the others jump.

runners_data.name: Liverpool Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for the Michael & David Easterby yard who won over 6f on Good and has four further placed runs on similar ground in fourteen attempts; Billy Garritty rides and the 23-day gap is fine, but at OR 68 he is towards the bottom of the handicap and needs the pace to be genuinely honest to run into the prize late.

runners_data.name: Slot
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's runner was on a racecourse just seven days ago and has twice finished second (on Good and Standard) — a naturally prominent racer who will find it very hard to get to the front in this field, meaning the quick turnaround may count for little if he cannot travel where he wants; his style fit is compromised and his best form has come when racing nearer the pace.

races.paceDynamic: Anaisa is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at York over 5½f, is set to stride into an uncontested lead from the gates with Sean Kirrane likely to dictate a sustainable rather than suicidal gallop. Behind her, Go Vince Go, Nursia, U S S Charleston, and Space Bear will all seek prominent positions, creating a genuine contest for the early places but not a pace meltdown — the gallop should be honest without being frantic. The field contains more naturally prominent types than the shape can accommodate: Dolos Dream, Dragon Spin, and Slot are all true front-rank horses that the race map has displaced into midfield, and of those three, Dolos Dream (Silvestre De Sousa) and Dragon Spin (Dougie Costello, twice a winner over 5f Good) are most likely to push forward and reclaim ground near the pace, while Slot will be forced to race in a role that does not suit. This setup — a controlled lead, a competitive scrimmage for the next few berths, and a compressed mid-division — favours horses who can travel prominently without being buried and quicken in the final furlong on fast ground; true hold-up horses will find traffic and a lack of a strong enough pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Anaisa Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Anaisa dictates a fair but unforced gallop and the prominent chasers settle within striking range.
scenarios.body: Anaisa sets the fractions from the front on Good to Firm ground that suits her, and the horses travelling just behind her in second or third position arrive with momentum at the 1f pole with minimal traffic to navigate. Space Bear, who has placed at 5f and 6f on fast ground and races prominently, and Go Vince Go, consistent at 5f in similar conditions, are ideally positioned to pounce from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Scrimmage, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the fight for prominent positions burns enough pace to bring genuine hold-up horses into the race late.
scenarios.body: Dragon Spin and Dolos Dream pushing forward from their displaced map positions adds competitive pressure to the early stages, stretching the field and setting up a finish for horses coming from off the pace in the final 1½f. Explosive Finnish (twice placed at 5f-6f Good/Firm) and Liverpool Star (a course winner at 6f Good) are the hold-up types best placed to benefit if the pace is genuinely sustained.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Midfielders Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion between displaced prominent types and natural midfielders creates a messy race that suits a horse finding a clear run late.
scenarios.body: With Dolos Dream, Dragon Spin, and Slot all wrestling for positions they cannot naturally secure, the middle of the field risks becoming bunched and difficult to navigate, opening a gap on the outside for a horse with a clear passage. Kinnalargy and Bravo Hotel, both hold-up types with placed form at 5f on Good, could profit if they find daylight at the critical moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Anaisa Outstays All, Wire to Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Anaisa is left completely alone on the front end and the gallop is slow enough that she simply pulses clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: At OR 81 she is not obviously well-handicapped, and her recent form figures of 4-5-4 suggest she tends to be overhauled late, so this outcome depends on the chasing pack failing to coordinate a challenge. A truly uncontested solo lead on fast ground is possible but unlikely given how many horses will push forward early.

watchPoints.text: Dragon Spin and Dolos Dream will both attempt to push forward from displaced midfield positions — watch the first furlong for a pace scramble that could unbalance Anaisa's intended lead and compress the entire field.

Slot's seven-day turnaround is tight even for a quick-recoverer, and if he is unable to get his natural prominent position his chance may evaporate before the race has properly developed — watch his early behaviour and any drifting in running.

Space Bear's trainer Michael Appleby has had zero winners from 22 runners in the past 14 days — not a form concern for the horse directly, but worth noting the yard's current cold spell before committing to his chance.

Liverpool Star and Explosive Finnish will be tracking from the hold-up pack and are the two horses most likely to benefit if the prominent scramble burns meaningful pace — watch their position at halfway relative to the leaders as an indicator of whether the race is truly run to suit finishers.

Good to Firm is the confirmed going for this 8:25 race despite earlier returns reading Good to Firm throughout the card — no degradation in surface speed is expected, which tilts further advantage toward horses that have produced their best form on fast ground specifically (Space Bear, Go Vince Go, Dragon Spin).
